step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates a serverless data processing pipeline at Autodesk. Data is ingested into S3 (13TB daily volume). S3 triggers an event notification via SNS, which invokes processing Lambda functions. The Lambda functions cleanse and enrich the data, then write metadata into DynamoDB. An ECS batch processing service reads metadata from DynamoDB, performs parquet batch conversion, and writes the resulting output back to S3 for end users. In case of processing errors, SNS triggers a secondary Lambda function that copies erroneous files to S3 for investigation.

graph.name: Autodesk Serverless Near-Real-Time Data Pipeline
graph.notes: Serverless pipeline replacing Spark-based data processing using S3, SNS, Lambda, DynamoDB, and ECS.

nodes.name: S3 Data Lake Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores raw ingested data (up to 13TB daily) and processed batch Parquet files.

nodes.name: SNS Topic
nodes.notes: Receives events from S3 and triggers processing and error-handling Lambdas.

nodes.name: Processing Lambda
nodes.notes: Cleanses, enriches data, and writes metadata to DynamoDB.

nodes.name: DynamoDB Metadata Store
nodes.notes: Provides high throughput and low latency for metadata operations.

nodes.name: ECS Batch Service
nodes.notes: Async RESTful Web API service that batches JSON outputs into Parquet format.

nodes.name: Error Handling Lambda
nodes.notes: Copies erroneous files back into S3 upon processing failures.

nodes.name: End Users
nodes.notes: Consumes processed Parquet data from S3.
